content.comment_body: Hello, I'm looking for advice. We have four [product_name] modules installed to control our four hydraulic lifeboat launch/recovery systems. Each module uses a protected red program card, so the program only operates when the card is present. Recently, two modules and their respective program cards failed. We replaced them with two new modules and cards, but these new cards are empty, so they won't run the modules. The existing cards still operate in the new modules. We attempted to access the program in the working cards, but pressing 'OK' for Edit displays 'Program Protect', preventing further access and no password is available. How can we copy the program from the working cards to the new ones? We lack computer-based programming software, and this installation appears entirely standalone with no digital backups. Any suggestions?

Hello, if you don't have a copy of the program (specifically, a backup using [product_name] programming software, not just the module's onboard program) then unfortunately there isn't a solution. The red card is designed for both copy and knowhow protection. Any program transferred from the module to these cards automatically receives this protection. You cannot upload the program; as you've noticed, if you remove the card, the module has no program. Additionally, a [product_name] PROM won't help because it cannot copy data from a protected red card. Your only option is to rebuild the program from scratch—be sure to create a backup this time.

Thank you for the explanation, [user_name]. What setup would be required to accomplish this onboard the ship? We have laptops, but presumably we'd need to acquire some programming software and a way to load it onto the cards or controller. A precise circuit diagram would also be essential. How would you approach the process? Do you have any idea what [company_name] might charge for the necessary equipment?

You will need: A) A complete version of [product_name] programming software, B) A programming cable to transfer your program from a PC to the module, and C) To try obtaining the program from your supplier, or be prepared to write the program yourself. The programming task isn't very difficult, but depending on the application, it may take considerable effort. A demo program is available from [company_name] free of charge, giving access to everything except transferring the program to the module. You can evaluate its functionalities in practice. [url]

Your last resort is likely to rewrite the program from scratch. I have a few questions: 1. Do you possess the circuit diagram? 2. Do you know the operating sequence for the machine? If you can answer YES to these, post here and I'll help you draft the program. Best of luck!

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced failures in two [product_name] controllers and their associated protected program cards for hydraulic system management. Due to copy and knowhow protection on the red cards, existing programs cannot be copied, edited, or transferred without an original project file or backup created with [product_name] programming software. Lack of digital backup and supporting documentation highlights critical constraints in program recovery and data handling when utilizing protected modules.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to recover and transfer a working program from a protected card to a new card or module, or to easily rebuild the lost configuration. They are looking for clear guidance or tools to avoid similar loss in the future.
